test_sse_c_encryption_roundtrip.detail: a transport-contract divergence, not an encryption defect. The request was accepted over plain http, which means the 32-byte customer key travelled in cleartext in the x-amz-server-side-encryption-customer-key header. AWS S3 refuses SSE-C over anything but HTTPS, and that requirement belongs to the SSE-C contract rather than to general transport policy, precisely because the key rides in a header. Otherwise the data path is correct: the object round-trips under the customer key (PUT echoed SSECustomerAlgorithm='AES256'), a read with no key is refused (HTTP 400 InvalidRequest: The object was stored using a form of Server Side Encryption. The correct parameters must be provided to retrieve the object.), a read with a different 32-byte key is refused (HTTP 400 InvalidRequest: The provided encryption parameters did not match the ones used originally to encrypt the object.), and the correct key with a mismatched key MD5 is refused (HTTP 400 InvalidRequest: The provided encryption parameters did not match the ones used originally to encrypt the object.).

no_key.message: The object was stored using a form of Server Side Encryption. The correct parameters must be provided to retrieve the object.

wrong_key.message: The provided encryption parameters did not match the ones used originally to encrypt the object.

The stacks run every system in its default single-node configuration with no key manager wired up, so this says nothing about whether the feature exists once one is.

test_object_lock_bucket_can_be_created.detail: CreateBucket accepted ObjectLockEnabledForBucket and GetObjectLockConfiguration answers HTTP 200, but the configuration it returns is {}. The header was accepted and ignored: the bucket has no object lock on it.

test_object_lock_legal_hold_blocks_delet.detail: the legal hold was accepted, then ignored: an object put with ObjectLockLegalHoldStatus=ON was deleted without error, it is gone afterwards, and GetObjectLegalHold reports None. The object also carries no version id, so there is no version behind the hold.

test_object_lock_retention_blocks_deleti.detail: the retention headers were accepted, then ignored: DeleteObject returned success while the retention still had ~119s to run, and the object is gone afterwards. A caller who set COMPLIANCE retention believes the object is immutable and it is not. The object also has no version id -- PutObject returned none and none is listed -- so there is no immutable version behind the key at all.

test_put_if_match_on_current_etag_succee.detail: the update was accepted with the current ETag, but a two-generations-stale ETag ("919c8b643b7133116b02fc0d9bb7df3f") is accepted just as readily (HTTP 200, object now b'third'). The header is being ignored, so this cell is not evidence of compare-and-swap support.

test_put_if_match_on_stale_etag_is_rejec.detail: stale If-Match ("d2edfbd157c1b22c42bedca6609130c7") accepted: the PUT returned HTTP 200 and the write landed on top of a version the client had never seen (object now b'second write - must not land'). A read-modify-write loop loses updates here without ever seeing an error.

test_put_if_none_match_allows_first_writ.detail: the conditional write was accepted on a new key, but repeating the identical If-None-Match: * PUT against the now-existing key is accepted too (HTTP 200, object is now b'second write - must not land'). The acceptance does not show the precondition was evaluated -- the header is being ignored, so this cell must not be read as conditional-write support.

test_put_if_none_match_rejects_overwrite.detail: precondition ignored: the second PUT returned HTTP 200 and the object was overwritten (now b'second write - must not land'). A lakehouse commit is lost here, silently -- the writer is told it succeeded.

test_sse_c_encryption_roundtrip.detail: the SSE-C headers are inert: the PUT echoed SSECustomerAlgorithm=None, and a GET carrying no key at all returns HTTP 200 and the plaintext (b'conformance payload'). The object is stored unencrypted while the caller believes it is encrypted under a key only they hold.

test_sse_s3_encryption_is_accepted.detail: the PUT was accepted and the body round-trips, but the object reports ServerSideEncryption=None. The encryption request was accepted and ignored, so a caller who asked for encryption at rest did not get it and was not told.
